licence.name: Site Terms and Conditions (Testimonium Ltd) — all rights reserved; no reuse grant; citation invited
licence.read_from: the Terms and Conditions text itself, 'Intellectual Property' section
licence.quote_le_15_words: are and will remain the exclusive property of the Company and its licensors
licence.grants_our_words: Nothing beyond reading. The site asks to be cited and provides the citation forms; a citation is a pointer, which is exactly what R1's pointer-only tier is.
licence.forbids_our_words: Copying the site's original content; use of its trademarks and trade dress without written consent. The laws/enforcement data is credited to a third-party database (Leiser, Santos & Doshi 2023) and so is doubly outside our reach.

permits_us: names-only — the 18 type NAMES plus a citation in one of the page's own forms; the one-sentence definitions are the site's original content and stay out of node text
why_our_words: The taxonomy names have become the field's vocabulary and appear in regulators' documents, so a node that says 'confirmshaming' with a pointer loses little. What we must not do is lift the definitions or the law-mapping counts. The legal obligations behind the patterns (DSA Art. 25, EDPB 03/2022) are already 'safe now' in R1's tiering and carry the enforceable text — that is where the obligation nodes' words should come from, not from here.
cheap_route_to_lift: Email legal@testimonium.co (address on the terms page) asking for permission to reproduce the 18 definitions with attribution. Price: one email; the site's stance on attribution suggests it is answerable.
unproven: Whether the earlier 2011-2023 versions of the site (old.deceptive.design) carried a different, more permissive notice — not fetched; irrelevant unless a node cites the old text. Price: one fetch.

pitfalls.what: The type names look generic enough to paraphrase, but the DEFINITIONS are one-sentence originals that a generator would happily reproduce as 'the definition of sneaking'. The membership rule must hold this family at names-only.
The anti-pattern detector idea (R1 §5b idea 4) needs definitions to detect against; if it takes them from this site it inherits this licence. Use the DSA/EDPB wording instead.
R1's item count (16) is stale against the page (18); a register that carries 16 names will miss Addictive Design and Currency Confusion.
pitfalls.owner: next source-register version (not R1's frozen assets)
